input: Shadow a local magistrate for my law studies

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the user's current stage of law studies (undergraduate, postgraduate, self-study, etc.) affects how formal the placement needs to be and what academic requirements it must satisfy.
The duration and number of sessions they want to shadow determines how much access they need to arrange and how far in advance they must plan.
Whether they already have a contact at a magistrates court or are starting from scratch completely changes the first steps of the plan.
The specific location or court they are targeting affects which body or authority they need to approach for permission.
Knowing if there is a fixed deadline (e.g., a coursework submission date or term end) shapes how urgently and in what sequence tasks must be completed.
Understanding whether this shadowing must result in a formal sign-off, a written reflection, a report, or simply personal learning affects what they need to document during the experience.
Knowing which area of law or type of case (criminal, civil, family, etc.) they most want to observe helps prioritise which court sittings or magistrates to target.

gold.taskTitle: Shadow a local magistrate for law studies
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to arrange and complete a magistrate shadowing experience as part of their law studies.

questions.title: What stage of law studies are you currently at?
questions.description: Establishes whether the user is an undergraduate, postgraduate, part of a vocational course, or self-studying — which determines how formal the placement must be.

questions.title: How many sessions or days do you want to shadow?
questions.description: Clarifies the intended duration and scale of the shadowing experience so the plan can account for the right amount of access to arrange.

questions.title: Do you already have a contact at a magistrates court?
questions.description: Determines whether the first step is leveraging an existing relationship or building one from scratch through a cold approach.

questions.title: Which town, city, or court are you hoping to shadow at?
questions.description: Identifies the specific court or geographic area so the correct authority or application process can be targeted.

questions.title: Is there a deadline this shadowing needs to be completed by?
questions.description: Uncovers any hard time constraints such as coursework due dates or term ends that would affect the urgency and sequencing of tasks.

questions.title: Does your course require a formal output from this shadowing?
questions.description: Establishes whether the user needs a signed attendance record, a written reflection, a report, or simply gains from the experience informally.

questions.title: Which type of case or legal area most interests you to observe?
questions.description: Identifies the user's preference for criminal, civil, family, or other proceedings so the right court sittings and magistrates can be prioritised.
